title: Remark
body_md:
In \cite{FKM1} the bound \eqref{nontrivialgeneric} was obtained for $q$ prime in the range \eqref{shortestd2} under the sole assumption that $\mathcal{F}$ is a Fourier sheaf (not geometrically isomorphic to the constant sheaf or any Artin--Schreier sheaf). label: mainthm2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{mainthm2}  Let $f(z)$ be a  Hecke eigencuspform  of level $1$ either holomorphic of weight $k\geqslant 2$ or a Laplacian eigenform with spectral parameter $t_f$; let $(\lambda_f(n))_{n\geqslant 1}$ be its Hecke eigenvalues. Let $\varphi$ be a Hecke--Maass cuspform for $\operatorname{GL}_{3,\mathbf{Q}}$ of level $1$ with Fourier coefficients $(\lambda_\varphi(n,r))_{n\geqslant 1,r\not=0}$.

Let $q=q_0q_1$ be a product of two distinct primes and let $$K_0:\mathbf{Z}/{q_0}\mathbf{Z}\mapsto \mathbf{C},\ K_1:\mathbf{Z}/{q_1}\mathbf{Z}\mapsto \mathbf{C}$$ be two complex valued functions which we identify with functions on $\mathbf{Z}$ of period $q_0$ and $q_1$ respectively;    we assume moreover that $K_0$ is the trace function attached to an $\ell$-adic middle extension Fourier sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbf{A}^1_{\mathbf{F}_{q_0}}$, geometrically irreducible and pure of weight $0$, of conductor $C_0$ and which is {\em good} in the sense of \cite[\S 1]{LMS}.  Let $K$ be the $q$-periodic function given by
$$
K(\cdot)=K_0(\cdot)K_1(\cdot).$$

Let $V\in \mathcal{C}^\infty_c(\mathbf{R})$ be a smooth function satisfying \eqref{bound-of-V}. Let $X\geqslant 1$ be such that $X\geqslant Z^4q^2q_0^{1/2}$. Then
\begin{multline}
	\label{d3x2boundcomposite}
	\sum_{n\geqslant 1,r\not=0}\lambda_\varphi(n,r)\lambda_f(n)K(nr^2)V\left(\frac{nr^2}{X}\right)\ll_{\varphi,f,\|K_1\|_\infty,C_0}X^{o(1)}Z^2\Bigg(X^{3/4}{q_0}^{3/4}\\
+
X^{\frac{2-\theta_3}{3-2\theta_3}}(q^2q_0^{1/2})^{\frac{1-\theta_3}{3-2\theta_3}}+\frac{X}{{q_0}^{1/4}}+ \frac{X^{3/4}q}{q_0^{1/2}}\Bigg).
                                                                      
	\end{multline}
Here $\theta_3=5/14$ is the best known bound towards the Ramanujan--Petersson conjecture on $\operatorname{GL}_3$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
In particular for $$q_0= q^{4/5+o(1)}$$ we obtain that
$$\sum_{n\geqslant 1,r\not=0}\lambda_\varphi(n,r)\lambda_f(n)K(nr^2)V\left(\frac{nr^2}{X}\right)\ll_{\varphi,f,\|K_1\|_\infty,C_0}X^{o(1)}Z^2\Bigg(X^{3/4}q^{3/5}+X^{\frac{2-\theta_3}{3-2\theta_3}}q^{\frac{12(1-\theta_3)}{5(3-2\theta_3)}}+\frac{X}{q^{1/5}}\Bigg)$$
and when $Z=1$ this bound is non-trivial {\rm(}i.e., \eqref{nontrivialgeneric} holds{\rm)} as soon as
$$X\geqslant q^{12/5+\delta}=q^{5/2-1/10+\delta}$$
for some $\delta>0$, in which case the second factor inside the parentheses can be removed.

title: Remark
body_md:
The exponent $1/364$ matches the one presented in \cite[Cor. 1.4]{Lin-Sun}. In that work, Q. Sun and the first named author obtained the following error term for the ``sharp cut" sum of the coefficients $\sum_{mr^2=n}\lambda_\varphi(m,r)\lambda_f(m)$
$$\sum_{nr^2\leqslant X}\lambda_\varphi(n,r)\lambda_f(n)=O\left(X^{\tau_6-1/364+o(1)}\right)$$
where
$$\tau_d=\frac{d-1}{d+1}$$ is the ``standard" exponent of Landau (see \cite[Prop. 1.1]{FICan}) for sharp-cut sums of coefficients of automorphic $L$-functions of degree $d$.

label: sqrootcancel
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{sqrootcancel} 
Let $T_\mathcal{F}({\mathbf{F}_q})$ be the subgroup of ${\mathbf{F}^\times_q}$ defined by
$$ T_\mathcal{F}({\mathbf{F}_q})=\{\lambda\in{\mathbf{F}^\times_q},\ [\times\lambda]^*\mathcal{F}\hbox{ is geometrically isomorphic to }\mathcal{F}\}.
$$
 Assuming that the sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is good, then for any $\alpha,\beta,\alpha',\beta',\gamma,\gamma',\delta\in{\mathbf{F}^\times_q}$, we have
$$\sum_{v}Z(v)\overline{Z'(v-\delta)}=O(q^{1/2}).$$
If $\delta=0$ the above bound holds unless
$$\alpha/\alpha'=\beta\gamma/\beta'\gamma'\in T_\mathcal{F}({\mathbf{F}_q})$$
in which case
$$\sum_{v}Z(v)\overline{Z'(v)}=c_\mathcal{F}(\alpha/\alpha')q+O(q^{1/2})$$
for $c_\mathcal{F}(\alpha/\alpha')$ some complex number of modulus $1$.
Here the implicit constants depend only on $C(\mathcal{F})$.
